strategy.summary: Reproduce the out-of-range integer defect in pandas maybe_convert_numeric and read_csv on the buggy commit 27368892d374 (Python 3.11.1, editable build with Cython, no-build-isolation). The developer's test test_convert_numeric_overflow in pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py should fail on the buggy revision because coerce_numeric=False raises ValueError('Integer out of range.') for 1<<65 and -(1<<65) (and their string forms), and pass on the fixed revision, which returns object dtype with exact Python ints. The companion read_csv and to_numeric tests in the same diff exercise the same path and should transition too. The reproduction depends on the C-level lib.maybe_convert_numeric, which is compiled, so the build must be redone for each revision.

pip_packages: numpy (latest release compatible with the checked-out pyproject; chosen here, not documented)
cython (version from the checked-out pyproject build-system requires)
pinned_because: numpy 1.24.1 was the version installed in issue#51295; the issue is evidence of the observed behaviour, not a documented constraint, so it is not required and is not used as a pin
pytest 7.2.1 from issue#51295 is not numerically relevant and is not pinned, to stay compatible with the test suite at this commit
no documented or era-table constraint exists for NumPy, so the NumPy choice is the strategy's own and should be stated when reporting results

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py pandas/tests/tools/test_to_numeric.py -k 'convert_numeric_overflow or int64_overflow or outside_int64_uint64_range or really_large' -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py::...::test_convert_numeric_overflow (parametrized over value in {-(1<<65), 1<<65, str(1<<65), '-'+str(1<<65)} and coerce_numeric in {False, True}); also pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py::test_int64_overflow and ::test_outside_int64_uint64_range with the python engine xfail removed; also pandas/tests/tools/test_to_numeric.py::test_really_large_scalar and ::test_really_large_in_arr
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 27368892d374, the four coerce_numeric=False parametrizations of test_convert_numeric_overflow raise ValueError 'Integer out of range.' and fail, and the python-engine read_csv cases fail because the xfail marks were removed while the parser still returns strings or raises. On the fixed revision, all parametrizations of test_convert_numeric_overflow pass (object dtype with exact ints for coerce_numeric=False, float dtype for coerce_numeric=True), and the read_csv and to_numeric tests pass. The transition from fail to pass on these tests is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: lib.maybe_convert_numeric(np.array([1<<65], dtype=object), set(), coerce_numeric=False) should return an object array holding the exact Python int 1<<65; on the buggy revision it raises ValueError.

input_output_examples.input: read_csv of a 'value' column containing 42 and 18446744073709551616.5, no dtype=

risks: The read_csv path (C engine versus python engine) decides whether the defect appears. The diff only removes xfail for the python engine, so the C engine may already pass; run both engines and report which one transitions.
The defect is in compiled code (lib.pyx). A stale build from the buggy commit will silently mask the fix, so rebuild after checking out the fixed revision.

The example 2^64+0.5 cannot be represented exactly as float64 (ulp at 2^64 is 4096), so the float64 expectation in the read_csv case depends on rounding, not on the 0.5; do not treat the float value as an exact oracle for that input.

No platform-specific or sanitiser-specific behaviour is evidenced; the reproduction assumes a 64-bit Linux or macOS environment with a standard CPython 3.11 build. If the failure only shows on 32-bit or a debug build, this plan will not reproduce it.
The PR date is null in the context, so the fixed revision cannot be identified by date; identify it from the PR merge commit instead of assuming it is the next commit.
The to_numeric test changes depend on the errors and kwargs parametrizations; if those fixtures differ from the diff's expectations, individual cases may fail for reasons unrelated to the bug.

oracle.reference_source: the developer's test assertions in pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py (tm.assert_numpy_array_equal against expected object or float arrays)
oracle.why: Expected values are exact Python ints for object dtype and exact powers of two for float (1<<65 is exactly representable), so exact equality is appropriate.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, the coerce_numeric=False cases call lib.maybe_convert_numeric on an out-of-range integer, which raises ValueError('Integer out of range.') before any assertion, so the test errors and fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, all eight parametrizations return the expected object or float arrays and tm.assert_numpy_array_equal succeeds, so the test passes.
